home.title: Nonsensical Battle Royale
home.subtitle: The question is... who's next?
home.tagline: Where Clue, Diplomacy, Werewolf, Among Us, and Machiavelli meet. An asynchronous social deduction game, played with real friends over real days. Accept your invite, and find out what fate has in store for you. Every round, everyone votes in secret on who doesn't make it to the next one.

iosInstall.title: Install this app
iosInstall.step1: Tap the Share icon in Safari's toolbar.
iosInstall.step2: Scroll down and tap "Add to Home Screen".
iosInstall.step3: Tap "Add" in the top-right corner to confirm.

threeDoors.title: The Three Doors
threeDoors.prologuePlaceholder: A short cinematic beat will set the scene here before the choice itself -- the corridor, the three doors, the sense that only one way out is real. Not written yet.
threeDoors.description: Three numbered doors, all labeled "Exit." Pick a door. If any two of you pick the same one, everyone loses. If all three picks are different, only one door was ever actually open -- whoever picked it is the sole survivor.
threeDoors.deadlineWarning: If not everyone has picked a door by the deadline, everyone still standing loses -- same as if two of you had picked the same door.

arrival.title: Arrival
arrival.storyPart1a: Having accepted the invitation, you travel to the mansion mentioned in the letter. On arrival you find your old friends, each one happier to see you than the last. There's laughter, drinks, old stories being retold, and no shortage of arguing over who sleeps where. The catching-up runs deep into the night, until everyone finally goes to bed.
arrival.storyPart1b: None of you suspect that this will be the last night anything still feels normal.
arrival.storyPart2a: Slowly, everyone wakes up. One by one, the guests drift into the kitchen -- coffee, hangovers, the usual morning-after murmur. But {gmName} is missing. Their seat at the table stays empty while the rest wonder where they've gotten to.
arrival.storyPart2b: One of you walks to the toilet -- and finds them there. Dead. Still half on the seat, pants around their ankles. A deep stab wound gapes in their neck; the blood has spread into a wide, dark pool across the tiles, reaching the walls and the sink. Their eyes are wide open, frozen in terror. The smell of blood hangs thick and sweet in the small, airless room. No doubt about it: this was no accident -- and whoever did it is still somewhere in this house.
arrival.waiting: Waiting for the rest of the house to arrive before the game can begin...

gmSetup.title: GM Setup
gmSetup.description: A short wizard walks through every setting, then lets you draft player invites -- the game itself is only created at the very end, once everything is decided.
gmSetup.minPlayersHint: Round 1 can't start until at least 5 players have accepted their invite, whichever start mode you pick below.
gmSetup.manualResolveHint: Regardless of resolution mode, you can always resolve a round early yourself once every alive player has voted.

basics.heading: Game basics
basics.gameNameHint: Identifies this game instance to you in the GM panel -- players never see it.
basics.displayNameHint: How you appear as the Game Master in narration and the end-of-game reveal -- doesn't have to be your real name.

rules.heading: Round rules
rules.roundIntervalHint: How long each round's voting window stays open before it resolves. 10 minutes minimum -- shorter than that can miss the automatic-resolve check, which runs every 5 minutes. Use a large number (e.g. 1440 for a full day) for an async game spread over days.
rules.missedDeadlineHintPrefix: What happens to a player who doesn't vote before the deadline.

missedDeadlineHints.forfeit_fatal: Missing the vote deadline eliminates that player, same as being voted out.
missedDeadlineHints.no_consequence: Missing the deadline does nothing beyond that player not casting a vote this round.
missedDeadlineHints.one_round_penalty: Missing the deadline excludes the player from voting and using powers next round only -- not eliminated.

rules.tieBreakHintPrefix: What happens when two or more players are tied for the most votes.

tieBreakHints.random: A random one of the tied players is eliminated, same as a real coin flip.
tieBreakHints.no_elimination: No one is eliminated this round -- the narration announces that everyone got lucky and lives to see another day.

round1StartHints.wait_for_all: Round 1 starts automatically the moment every invited player has redeemed their invite.
round1StartHints.gm_manual: Round 1 only starts when you click "Start Round 1" yourself, whenever you're ready.
round1StartHints.scheduled: Round 1 starts automatically at a time you set, regardless of who has accepted. Anyone who hasn't redeemed their invite by then is excluded from the game entirely.

rules.roundResolutionHintPrefix: How every round after the first one ends.

roundResolutionHints.manual: Rounds only resolve when you click "Resolve now" yourself, even after the deadline passes.
roundResolutionHints.automatic: Rounds resolve on their own the moment the deadline passes -- no need to have the app open.

rules.allowVoteChange: Allow players to change their vote
rules.allowVoteChangeHint: If off (default), a vote is final the moment it's cast. If on, a player can re-vote as many times as they want before the round resolves -- only their latest vote(s) count.
rules.threeDoorsDeadlineMinutesHint: How long the Three Doors endgame stays open once it starts. If not every remaining player has picked a door by this deadline, everyone still standing loses -- same as a collision.

powers.heading: Hidden powers & bots
powers.doubleVoteEnabledHint: On by default. Each round, one random alive player is secretly given a second vote -- they're told privately and never have to disclose it. This is part of the game's hidden powers system: players are never told it exists, they only discover it by experiencing it.
powers.doubleVoteRound1Disclaimer: Never handed out in round 1, regardless of this setting -- no one has proven anything yet, so there's nothing to reward with extra voting power that early. The earliest a double vote can appear is round 2.
powers.doubleVoteFloorRoundsHint: How many recent rounds' holders are excluded when picking who gets it next, so the same player isn't re-picked too soon. Falls back to picking from everyone alive if excluding recent holders would leave no one eligible (e.g. a very small player count). Default 2. Set to -1 for a stricter rule instead: each player can hold the double vote at most once for the entire game -- once everyone's had a turn, no one gets it again for the rest of the game (no fallback).
powers.botModeHint: Fills the game with algorithm-controlled players (random moves for now) so you can test a full game solo. You still need at least one real player besides yourself -- bots supplement a game, they don't replace it.
powers.botCountHint: How many bots to add alongside the real players you invite (max 19, and bots + real players together should stay within the 20-player ceiling).

miniGames.heading: Mini-games
miniGames.moveToRoomEnabledHint: Every round, alive players may move one step through the mansion and guess where another player is hiding. Correct guesses earn the guesser a point.

access.heading: Access
access.setupSecretHint: A shared secret that proves you're allowed to create a game -- separate from the invite links you'll send players.

invites.heading: Invites
invites.description: Draft the players you want to invite. Nothing is actually created yet -- these become real invites only once you create the game below.
invites.noneYetHint: No invites drafted yet -- that's fine (e.g. a bot-only test game), or add one below.
